sources_skipped.description: Only populated when `sources` was not given (an unrestricted search). Adapters registered in this deployment (feature flag on) that were not queried because they are not currently usable (missing/invalid credentials). `web_scraper` never appears here: it makes no upstream call and its empty result is by design, not a skip. Empty together with total=0 means every adapter this deployment could run, ran, and found nothing.
sources_skipped.title: Sources Skipped

sources_unknown.description: Sources named in the request that were not queried: either no such adapter exists in this deployment (e.g. a typo) or it is registered but switched off (feature flag or missing credentials). The registry cannot tell those apart honestly, so both land here. Empty on a genuine no-hit — [] together with total=0 means the requested sources ran and found nothing. Not a failure: adapters that ran and errored appear in sources_failed instead.
sources_unknown.title: Sources Unknown

info.description: Standalone federated media search service. Provides federated search across YouTube, Vimeo, podcasts, Wikimedia, and web sources, with transcript extraction, playlist import, collections, downloads, and quality scoring. Auth via license-token introspection (X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <token>); trusted-network bypass for in-cluster traffic.

post.description:
Always 501 — see ``_NOT_IMPLEMENTED_DETAIL``.

Deliberately raises *before* touching the database, so no row is written:
a persisted "pending" job is the artefact that made this dishonest. The
validation that used to run here (400 on an empty ``item_ids``) is gone on
purpose — negotiating the payload of a request that can never be serviced
would be the same phantom contract in miniature.

``DownloadManager.create_jobs`` is left intact as the (tested) persistence
layer a future worker will drive; wiring that worker is what re-opens this
route.

get.description:
Find items related to the given item.

Semantic-first: when the item has an embedding (populated at ingest), rank
same-tenant candidates by cosine similarity of their embeddings. Falls back
to the metadata heuristic (same media_type / author, newest) when the item
has no embedding yet or has no embedded neighbours — so old rows and
embed-unavailable states still return something useful.
get.summary: Find items related to a given item

get.description:
Read the quality score of a single media item.

Read-only counterpart to ``POST /{item_id}/score``, which recomputes AND
persists. This route never writes: it returns the score already stored on
the item, and for an item that has never been scored it computes one
in-memory and returns it *without* persisting. Use POST to store a score.
get.summary: Read the quality score of a single media item

post.description:
Compute quality score for a single media item.

Recomputes the score and PERSISTS it onto the item. For a read that does
not write, use ``GET /{item_id}/score``.

get.description:
Health check -- queries backend services and returns aggregate status.

Deliberately stays HTTP 200 regardless of aggregate status. This path is the
Deployment's ``startupProbe`` target; a 503 here on a dependency outage would
exhaust ``failureThreshold`` and kill the container before it ever starts.
The verdict is carried in the ``status`` body field for dashboards/humans;
the kubelet's not-ready verdict belongs to ``/health/ready``.

Liveness probe -- always returns alive.

Deliberately unconditional 200: it answers "is this process still serving
HTTP", nothing more. Making liveness depend on upstreams would restart-loop
every pod during an upstream outage (killing a healthy process fixes
nothing and destroys in-flight work). Dependency state is readiness' job.

Readiness probe -- checks the database (the only critical dependency).

Returns 200 when the database answers, 503 otherwise, so the
kubelet readiness probe can actually pull the pod out of Endpoints during a
dependency outage. The body keeps the ``ReadinessStatus`` shape unchanged
for non-kubelet consumers.

Postgres is this service's own state store, so every non-probe route
depends on it.

Lightweight status endpoint for gateway proxy health checks.

Deliberately unconditional 200: it performs no dependency checks at all, so
there is nothing that could make it 503. It exists purely so a gateway can
confirm the route is reachable.
